title: Modular Inverse
prompt:
Find the modular inverse of 20 modulo 29
(the x in [0, 29) with 20*x ≡ 1 (mod 29)).
hint: use the extended Euclidean algorithm; enter one integer in [0, m)
recap:
The modular inverse of a (mod m) is the x with a·x ≡ 1 (mod m); it exists iff gcd(a, m) = 1. The extended Euclidean algorithm finds (x, y) with a·x + m·y = 1, so x mod m is the inverse. For prime m, Fermat gives a⁻¹ ≡ a^(m-2).

Example — 3⁻¹ mod 7: 3·5 = 15 ≡ 1 (mod 7), so it is 5.

Reference: CLRS §31.4.
